India needs strong homegrown businesses to become a wealthy and powerful nation, argues entrepreneur and author Jaithirth Jerry Rao. Drawing on Mahatma Gandhi’s ties with industrialists such as G.D. Birla and Jamnalal Bajaj, Rao says India has a long history of vilifying its business leaders. From Reliance’s global refining ambitions to Adani’s strategic port investments in Israel and Australia, he argues that conglomerates should be nurtured as national assets, not treated as villains.
